name: Iteration Plan
one_liner: One iteration, one plan: the goal, the items, and how.
purpose: In its minimal form the Iteration Plan is the subset of the Work Items List planned for the upcoming iteration, with the iteration start and end dates, the Iteration Goal defined by the Product Owner and committed to by the A-PCT, and every work item needed to achieve that goal. It may also capture synchronisation points with other teams and the issues and risks to be solved during the iteration. It helps the team monitor progress — with an iteration Kanban board and burndown charts — and keeps the iteration's results for later assessment based on the Iteration Review's outputs.

fields.what: Defined by the Product Owner and committed to by the A-PCT; the single thing the iteration is trying to achieve.
fields.pollux: Iteration 9: 'Finance can reconcile portal totals to the accounts without a spreadsheet.'

fields.what: The iteration's timebox — fixed dates, with scope actively managed to meet them rather than the reverse.
fields.pollux: Iteration 9 runs 07–18 May 2029; the two-week timebox never moves.

fields.f: Subset of the Work Items List
fields.what: The set of work items — a subset of the WIL — planned for the upcoming iteration.
fields.who: PrOw Consulted for the prioritised WIL
fields.pollux: Nine items pulled from the top of Curie's list, worth 34 points.

fields.what: The list of all work items that must be delivered to achieve the Iteration Goal — not merely the highest-priority ones.
fields.pollux: WIL-033 reconciliation plus BUG-112 rounding, because reconciliation is meaningless while the bug stands.

fields.what: Work items are decomposed into the tasks required to complete them, each taken and estimated by a team member.
fields.pollux: Babbage took the reconciliation query tasks; Lamarr took the panel and its accessibility work.

fields.what: Availability in hours per member, net of holidays and unplanned-event allowance, determines what can be committed.
fields.pollux: Eight members, nine working days, seven hours, minus 10% for unplanned work.

fields.what: Points where the iteration depends on other teams, especially teams in different projects.
fields.pollux: CASTOR extract freeze window shared with Lending Operations for the whole iteration.

fields.what: The plan is also used to refer to issues, risks and similar items that must be solved during the iteration.
fields.pollux: Issue: Finance's rule set arrived two days late, recorded against iteration 9.

fields.what: Initialised from the Iteration Planning inputs and updated constantly to reflect planned versus achieved work.
fields.pollux: Updated daily after the stand-up; flat first three days exposed the late rule set.

fields.what: An iteration Kanban board visualising the scope and state of the iteration's work items.
fields.pollux: Board in the team space at Kirchberg; Gantt visits it instead of asking for a schedule.

fields.what: Provides an indicator of the team's current progress and a forecast for completion of the iteration's work.
fields.pollux: Forecast at day 6 showed the scenario spike would not finish; it was dropped, not extended.

fields.what: Work items can be part of a feature — a functional unit representing a recognisable and valuable part of the solution.
fields.pollux: Iteration 9 items all belong to feature F2, instrument and maturity views.

fields.what: Once items are assigned the team completes all of them regardless of original priorities, except blocking dependencies with other teams.
fields.pollux: The 3-point bug is finished alongside the 13-point story; neither is 'the important one'.

fields.what: Every iteration starts with Iteration Planning and ends with the Iteration Review; that is captured in one unique plan.
fields.pollux: Thirty-nine iteration plans over POLLUX's eighteen months, each self-contained.

fields.what: Not static: the burndown must reflect the current situation and iteration scope may be revised mid-iteration.
fields.pollux: Scope revised on day 6 of iteration 9 when the scenario spike was dropped.

fields.what: The Review's conclusions — goal achieved or not, items not delivered and why — are recorded as part of the plan.
fields.pollux: Iteration 9 closed: goal achieved, one item carried over, retrospective actions logged separately.

fields.what: Before compiling this by hand, investigate software tools that may save a significant amount of time.

traps: PrOw is Consulted here but Supports on the Release Plan.
Iteration Plan = how; Release Plan = what and when.
The Iteration Goal is the PrOw's; the plan is the TeCo's.
Inside an iteration, original item priorities stop mattering — everything committed gets done.
Iteration burndown tracks effort; release burndown tracks functionality.
